Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, Park and Activities Commission Members will be

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
Meeting ID: 825 4537 7919 , Meeting Password: 449726. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using
the call-in option from a phone line.)

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”
page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an
“eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp
page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen
by the public, will be considered by the Commission and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by
entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 825 4537 7919, Meeting Password: 449726.

- Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The Meeting Host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's
website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ADJOURNED MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 20, 2021

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 7:02 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
  Executive Order N-29-20.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Bain, McCormick, Persichina, Pope, Retz,
  Romanelli, and Ciarolla (joined at 7:11 pm)

  Commissioners Absent:  None

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Daniel A-Haja

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING DRAFT MINUTES
  OF AUGUST 16, 2021

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  B.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING REVISED
  MINUTES OF JULY 19, 2021

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  None

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja provided a brief overview of the staff
  report.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked why the additional charge for judging the parade
  was applied. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja explained that the scores
  accrued by the parade units apply to their standing for that year’s Rose Float
  Parade.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  RECOMMENDATION TO CITY COUNCIL TO ENTER INTO THE
  ATTACHED AGREEMENT WITH PAGEANTRY PRODUCTIONS TO
  PROVIDE PARADE MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR THE PENINSULA
  HOLIDAY PARADE OF LIGHTS ON DECEMBER 4, 2021.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
SEPTEMBER 20, 2021
   There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  B.  GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER - FUTURE FACILITY USE CONTINUED
  DISCUSSION

  Assistant City Manager (ACM) Davis provided a brief overview of the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ asked if nighttime nature walks would still go forward at
  the facility if events were not allowed past 8 pm. ACM Davis noted that activity is
  hosted by the Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy (PVPLC) operation
  agreement which would continue.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if a school could still hike at the canyon while PVPLC
  was running one of their programs. ACM Davis responded that use by one
  organization at a time would only apply to City rentals of the facility, in the case the
  City is renting out to two separate organizations.

  CHAIR POPE noted the change in the opening and closing times and asked for
  clarification on the hours proposed, setting of the hours and monitoring usage of
  the facility. ACM Davis responded that the hours suggested take into consideration
  how the facility is currently being used under the PVPLC and how the City Council
  Chamber is used. ACM Davis shared that because of City Hall business hours and
  meetings the Council Chamber is limited to the evening hours up until 10 pm and
  noted the Council Chamber is not adjacent to a neighborhood. She also noted that
  the intent is not for it to be a revenue generating venue but rather a community
  facility.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted the difficulty of closing the facility at 8 pm explaining
  it may be difficult for community group meeting attendees. She also asked if there
  were any offsite parking or shuttling possibilities if needed. ACM Davis stated
  recommended rental hours will be brought to the City Council for consideration.
  She added that the parking would be handled by staff reviewing applications and
  with certain conditions required before approved facility use, including the
  consideration if additional parking is needed that could require a reciprocal
  agreement or shuttling for offsite parking. ACM Davis stated that there will
  ultimately be new parking established when Butcher Park is developed and there
  is existing parking across the street at Dapplegray Park as well.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ noted Dapplegray HOA used the prior community center
  for its homeowner’s association meetings which began at 7 pm and can sometimes
  go as late as 9 or 10 pm; he and expressed interest in seeing the new site being
  available later than 8 pm. COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK and CHAIR POPE
  agreed that a 9 pm or 10 pm closing time is ideal but can initially begin with 9 pm
  and adjust as needed.

  CHAIR POPE stated that a report on usage and rental inquiries should return within
  three to six months upon opening to address any issues and consider if
  modifications need to be made.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted that there may interest among
  organizations to have alcohol permitted depending on the type of event and
  suggested that it be revisited in the future after opening.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN endorses use of the facility for small receptions and social
  gatherings within the approved times along with amplified sound indoors. She
  suggests starting with no alcohol and seeing if there is a demand for it.
  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA agrees with not allowing alcohol for a year unless
  demand is high, and the City can revisit the issue.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 20, 2021
   CHAIR POPE requested staff develop a way to track rental requests and inquires
  to be used in a report back to the Commission and Council.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted that since Ernie Howlett Park allows alcohol
  for special events under certain approvals which would make it consistent with if
  permitted at new nature center through an approval process.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if the facility would be open to non-resident groups.
  CHAIR POPE suggested a non-resident pricing model. ACM responded the facility
  would be open to non-resident groups with a proposed fee structure between
  resident/non-resident.

  CHAIR POPE noted the proximity of the Nature Center to resident homes compared
  to Ernie Howlett as a basis to keep the restriction of alcohol initially.

  ACM Davis summarized the consensus of the Commission was to recommend the
  hours of 9 am opening and closing at 9 pm or 10 pm, provide a report of usage
  within six months and after the first year of operations as well as a review of interest
  from applicants that do not meet the eligibility guidelines, and include any inquiries
  that request alcohol be permitted.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked about parking solutions. ACM Davis
  responded that if more than 60 parking spots would be needed, the facility user
  could be required to provide a parking plan to the City as part of the approval
  process.

  Consensus of the Commission to share input received with the City Council for
  future consideration.

  C.  HIGHRIDGE PARK MURAL PROJECT

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja provided a brief overview of the staff
  report.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ approved the title “Community Buzz” for one side of the
  bulletin. COMMISSIONERS BAIN and ROMANELLI agreed.

  CHAIR POPE asked if the corkboard on the “Community Buzz” would cause
  damage to the artwork. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja noted the artwork
  could be coated with a clear coat to prevent damage to the artwork. Audience
  Member Marianna DeSalles noted the increased bulletin board size could decrease
  damage to nearby artwork.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked about the design of the blue area used in the
  artwork. Ms. DeSalles noted blue and orange were opposite of each other on the
  color wheel. COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if one side would have cork board and
  the other with only artwork. Ms. DeSalles noted the addition of cork board at the
  last meeting upon the Commission’s direction.

  CHAIR POPE suggested weaving the additional phrases (“Bee Kind” “Buzz
  Bulletin”) within the artwork.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ wanted a clarification of the enlargement of the cork board.
  Ms. DeSalles suggested a 20% increase in size and agreed the corkboard would
  be enlarged and the blue area would be reduced.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked about the finances and suggested a 10%
  contingency be considered in addition to the cost of $5,300.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 20, 2021
   COMMISSIONER RETZ moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  MOVE FORWARD WITH THE ART AS PRESENTED WITH “COMMUNITY
  BUZZ” AND A 20% INCREASE TO THE SIDE AND LOWER SECTION OF
  THE CORK BOARD AND TO INCREASE THE BUDGET BY 10% OVER
  THE $5,300 AS A NOT TO EXCEED NUMBER.

  AYES:  Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina, Pope, Retz, Romanelli
  ABSENT:  None

  The motion carries.

  D.  PENINSULA EDUCATION FOUNDATION - EVENT PROPOSAL

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the staff report.

  VICE CHAIR CIAROLLA asked if the event planned on using the landfill to shuttle
  attendees to the event. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja shared that they are
  not using the landfill and that they are planning on having spaces for VIPs and general
  attendees at the park but organizing drop-offs for those utilizing ride shares.

  Kelly Cook, a representative from the Peninsula Education Foundation (PEF), noted
  they are working with Uber and Lyft to offer a discount code for ride share users. The
  parking lot at the park would be used. ACM Davis asked if the grass bowl area would
  be available for extra parking. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja responded
  that the lot next to the city yard and longitudinal parking would be sufficient for the
  event.

  CHAIR POPE asked if the youth sports would be affected with the parking.

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja noted there would be no ball play at the time
  and AYSO would take only the left side of the park rather than the parking lot area
  closest to the horse rings.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked if parking would take place on the fields.
  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja responded that the only areas used for
  parking would be the lot and possibly the grass bowl area.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if it was possible to provide a bird’s eye view
  of the park so PEF could notate parking and entry ways of the proposed event. CHAIR
  POPE agrees with the proposal of the event layout.

  CHAIR POPE asked if the application could be accepted with an acceptable parking
  solution and event layout to be provided to staff before the event. Kelly Cook
  responded that they would provide a map of the parking area with CAD drawing
  assistance.

  ACM Davis stated that the City could provide a map that the PEF could use.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER BAIN, TO:

  APPROVE THE APPLICATION BY THE PENINSULA EDUCATION
  FOUNDATION TO HOST THEIR EVENT AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK ON
  NOVEMBER 6, 2021, FROM 12:00 PM - 5:00 PM.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  E.  2021 HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE DEBRIEF

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 20, 2021
   Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noted making the race a sanctioned 10k race would
  be difficult due to the trail and length covered.

  CHAIR POPE asked if this is an event the City can run without a race director. ACM
  Davis agreed that it would be feasible.

  F.  TRACY AUSTIN DOUBLES TOURNAMENT (VERBAL REPORT)

  ACM Davis noted the event will be moving forward and is scheduled for November
  12-14. She stated that Tracy and her husband shared that tennis has flourished
  during the pandemic, so we are anticipating a good turnout. She further explained that
  staff is looking to make the event more user-friendly with online features and working
  with our long-time tennis pro, Bob Krueger.

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja noted using the USTA website to register
  and receive payments will provide a smoother experience to the players.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN suggested having a lot of advance communication with
  players as the event will take place in two separate places and can cause confusion.

  G.  BUTCHER PARK UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  ACM Davis noted the City entered contract in June with the landscape architect that
  provided the conceptual design and a contract with Wildan who is conducting an
  engineering assessment; Wildan has completed their field survey and now have their
  base plan with the existing conditions. She explained that the next step is a kickoff
  with the landscape architect and then creation of the final plan with specifications. She
  stated that the project is budgeted and expected to break ground within this fiscal
  year.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked what the Water District was proposing. ACM Davis
  responded that a reservoir project was initiated with the Butcher Park corner
  requested for staging a few years ago. The area is not approved to use for staging
  currently.

  H.  CITY CELEBRATION UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  ACM Davis noted that the event is scheduled to occur September 25th with no
  restrictions per COVID event guidelines for outdoor events with less than 10,000
  people. She continued that due to public health concerns the corn and hay pits will
  not be available this year. The standard hayrides, pony rides and petting zoo will be
  at the event along with a new rock-climbing attraction.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN and VICE CHAIR CIAROLLA noted not receiving the event
  postcard invitations. ACM Davis noted extras are available at City Hall for those who
  did not receive it.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted not being able to attend the morning volunteer shift but
  volunteered for the afternoon shift. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI also volunteered
  for an afternoon shift in the Pepper Tree Foundation booth.

  7.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked about a bid for the poison ivy removal at
  George F Canyon. ACM Davis responded that she would get back to the

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
SEPTEMBER 20, 2021
   Commission with an answer.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked for an update on the median near
  Dapplegray and Strawberry Lanes. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI responded
  that it was a continuation of Bennett Landscape and is still being worked on.

  CHAIR POPE gave an update regarding the Taber Grove dedication and noted that
  it was well-attended.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  a. HONORING DALE ALLEN

  CHAIR POPE made remarks honoring Dale Allen upon his passing in August
  and spoke of his accomplishments and his impact on the community.
  COMMISSIONER RETZ and PERSICHINA shared personal stories and
  accounts of Mr. Allen and his impact on the community.

  8.  STAFF ITEMS

  None

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF AUGUST 24, 2021

  Received and filed.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  ROCKBLUFF PLAYGROUND

  None

  B.  CHANDLER PARK PLAYGROUND

  None

  C.  PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER CONTRACT RENEWAL

  None

  11.  ADJOURNMENT

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA moved, seconded  by  COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 8:32 PM TO THE NEXT ADJOURNED
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON OCTOBER 19, 2021
  AT 7:00 P.M., WHICH BE HELD VIA TELECONFERENCE.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  ___________________________
  Daniel A-Haja  Lisa Van Ingen Pope
  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
SEPTEMBER 20, 2021
